summary: Feed s151_double to NDR is degraded: 5.6% TCP packet loss (159/2860) exceeds 1% threshold and 94.0% of frames are GRE-encapsulated, hiding inner traffic from NDR that requires both directions and full payload for detection.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker or SPAN buffer oversubscription causing ~5.6% TCP sequence gaps. Tool overload check is healthy, so drops occur before the tool (broker ingress/SPAN), not at NDR ingress policer.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR cannot reassemble TCP streams, misses payload and flow state, leading to missed detections, broken session reconstruction, and false negatives despite needing full payload and bidirectional flows.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute flows across multiple 10G NDR interfaces to eliminate broker drops while preserving flow affinity required for bidirectional NDR analysis. If source is SPAN, also migrate to TAP with aggregation.

findings.root_cause: 2780 of 2958 frames (94.0%) arrive inside GRE tunnel and are forwarded encapsulated. Packet broker is not stripping GRE, so NDR sees only outer tunnel headers.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR sees only outer GRE/IP headers and cannot parse inner IP/TCP/UDP or application payload, blinding detection for 94% of traffic despite needing full payload inspection.

recommended_fix.why: Terminate/strip GRE at packet broker and forward inner packets to NDR so it can perform full L3-L7 inspection and bidirectional flow correlation.
